 Dabo Swinney gambled on his QBs...and lost
 Heading into today’s action, a lack of foresight was exposed. 
 Dabo Swinney gambled on his QBs...and lost
 Grayson Mann  ·  Staff Writer  ·  1 day ago 1 day ago 
 ios_share Share 
 f 
 X 
 SMS 
 @ 
 CLEMSON - Dabo Swinney stood confidently at the podium in Charlotte at ACC Kickoff.
 Clemson didn't need a "shiny" quarterback from the transfer portal, and if it didn't work out, they'd be raked over the coals for it.
 Those coals are hot now.
 The 6-4 Tigers, fresh off an embarrassing 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech, have plenty of flaws.
 Play calling. Struggles up front. Inconsistencies in the run game.
 A flaw louder than all of that was entirely avoidable.
 Regardless of what we know now, Clemson's quarterback room once included Christopher Vizzina , Tait Reynolds , Brock Bradley , Trent Pearman , and Chris Denson .
 You could've argued that maybe the Tigers had enough in the room to make something happen with the return of Chad Morris .
 Hesitation, on the other hand, was also entirely fair.
 Back on national signing day, Swinney was asked whether he was considering bringing in a quarterback to compete for the job.
 Here was his full answer:
 "We just signed two to come compete, and we got Denson here to compete, and, you know, we got CV, who's really only played one true game, you know, from a start standpoint, who's here to compete. This kid's done his part, and he's been waiting his time, and now it's his time. Now he's got to win the job. I mean, obviously, he's kind of where you start, but he's got to win it. Same thing with Denson. I mean, Denson didn't come here just to stand on the sideline. He came here to compete, so let's go compete."
 Denson isn't just standing on the sideline. He's standing with the wide receivers after switching positions this spring, and has two wildcat carries for a whopping three yards.
 It took Clemson a few weeks in the spring to realize Denson didn't have what it takes to compete.
 Denson was with the team for over a year prior to this, which begs the question: did just two extra weeks of spring practice really swing a position change?
 That's just one part of the equation.
 The writing was on the wall: this would eventually become a battle between Christopher Vizzina and Tait Reynolds .
 Between the two entering the fall, they had one combined start: Vizzina looked solid, tossing three touchdowns against SMU, although the Mustangs' pass defense was second-to-last in the country in 2025.
 Reynolds missed his entire senior season due to a hamstring injury, and even before that, he looked like a raw prospect who needed to sit first before he was truly ready.
 Even if you believe Vizzina or Reynolds is the next Deshaun Watson or Trevor Lawrence in waiting, how do you not grab a quarterback in the portal to supplement depth, or for the worst-case scenario?
 Any Trent Pearman rebuttal died with multiple interceptions against Charleston Southern and three poor drives against Georgia Tech.
 Speaking of worst-case scenarios, the Tigers’ 20-6 loss to the Yellow Jackets was that doomsday event.
 Reynolds went down on Clemson’s first drive, and out came Pearman.
 Heading into today’s action, a lack of foresight was exposed.
 Pearman looked outmatched, and it took three drives for Swinney to turn to Vizzina, who was clearly hobbled and limping after each throw, essentially being set up to fail as a last resort.
 The offense put up the lowest total of the year, and it felt even worse.
 Clemson has two losses this year that fall squarely on a gamble that’s wasted a season that felt promising.
 Virginia Tech proved Tait Reynolds wasn’t quite ready.
 Georgia Tech proved Clemson’s lack of portal foresight would be the final dagger in a season full of fatal wounds.
 Swinney took a gamble. It’s cost Clemson dearly.
 When he took to the podium in Charlotte, he knew if his decision backfired, they’d rake him over the coals, and those coals are hot now.
 Clemson’s 20-6 loss said plenty about the state of affairs in Tiger Town, and none of those were very positive.  I have sat in those stands for 50 years...sat through some  nmiserable teams and miserable coaches. Ford was the one bright light but the trustees snuffed that out. Then the downhill spiral to Bowden who started bringing the offense back up. We had no defense. Finally people had enough of the bubble screen from Rob Spence who took over after Rich Rod. I think TB couldve saved his job by letting Spence go but I understand they were church buddies. Enter Dabo-handpicked by the players. He created a juggernaut within the confines of the rules. The rules have now changed and failure to adapt=extinction in any situation  During all that time we got beat down for a long time. We knew why and we expected it so in some ways, it wasnot as painful. Now we are at a period of staleness again. Some coaches need to go--as GT did. Chad Morris was a disaster hire. if you have an 8 inch playbook but can only run four-that's pathetic. he needs to be in the box. The OL gets beat mentaly and physically. Our RBs run not to the hole but into the pile. Now there's too much pressure on this team and we will likely finish from here at 0-2. One good thing-if you are an avid fan you can probably up your IPTAY donation and get good parking places. People will not put up with this craps. The 1970s are gone and 2026 is just plain EMBARRASSING
